 Silver’s sharp correction brings buyers back to the market

 Priya Kothari / Nov 18, 2026, 00:46 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print The steep correction may improve retail demand in the short term, particularly among consumers waiting for a price drop Pune: Silver prices have dipped nearly 57% to Rs1.7 lakh per kg (excluding GST) after touching record highs of Rs4 lakh per kg in Jan. The sharp correction has brought some relief to buyers and manufacturers grappling with elevated prices. “We are seeing selling activity in the market from investors, because people feel that silver prices will drop further. However, there might be an increase in prices after a brief dip,” said Anil Jain , a jeweller at Mumbai’s Zaveri Bazaar. The steep correction may improve retail demand in the short term, particularly among consumers waiting for a price drop. “The gold-silver ratio is around 82, up from about 46 at Jan’s peak, so silver now looks cheap next to gold. The risks are real, though. Industrial demand is softening, and photovoltaic silver use is projected to decline by about 19%. Over the next four to six weeks, I expect silver to consolidate between $44 and $53/oz, or about Rs1,58,000–1,90,000/kg on MCX,” said Dr Renisha Chainani, chief research officer at Augmont. The gold-to-silver ratio represents how many ounces of silver it takes to buy a single ounce of gold. However, market volatility continues to remain a concern. Silver prices are influenced by several global factors, including industrial demand, investment activity, currency movements and broader economic developments. “These factors can contribute to fluctuations in the market, making short-term price movements difficult to anticipate. Rather than focusing on near-term movements, consumers should approach their purchases with a longer-term perspective and align them with their financial goals and investment horizon,” said Samit Guha, managing director & CEO of MMTC-PAMP. The dip has brought some buyers back to the market, although many remain cautious about making large purchases. Jewellers said customers were increasingly enquiring about silver coins, bars and smaller denominations, with some preferring to make staggered purchases rather than commit to bulk buying amid expectations of further volatility.  Parag Vora, a jeweller at Camp, said investors are in a wait-and-watch mode considering the uncertainties on the macroeconomic front. “We are bullish on silver. There is expectation that it may cross the Rs2–2.5 lakh mark next year,” he said. Shruti Panjwani, a Wanowrie resident, had sold some silver when prices were hovering around the Rs2.5 lakh mark. “I am now actively buying silver coins and silver in smaller denominations since the price has fallen. Let’s see how prices move,” she said. Financial advisers are informing clients to keep silver to 5–10% of the portfolio. “We have told clients to stagger purchases over the next six months or so. They should hold for at least 2–3 years to gain substantially. Silver ETFs are also a good option as they are cheaper than physical gold,” said a personal wealth manager at Fatimanagar.
